note: TAF4 loss-of-function variants cause autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder with facial dysmorphisms and developmental delay, and transcription pause/release dysregulation is an established mechanism in overlapping neurodevelopmental disorders.

evidence.text: De novo putative loss-of-function variants in TAF4 cause a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder featuring intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD). Common features include intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms.

evidence.text: Disruption of transcription pause and escape is linked to neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by intellectual disability, short stature, and related dysmorphisms.

source.title: Transcription pause and escape in neurodevelopmental disorders
